title: Soveraeign Service Manifest
description: One bounded service's declared surface. Each operation states the record it acts on, the append-preserving CRUD verb it realizes, its logical endpoint, the preconditions it checks, what a commit produces, and every refusal it may return. Office placement, required authority, effect class, and actor kinds are NOT declared here; contracts/capability-offices.json owns those and the capability map joins the two. A manifest grants nothing: it describes a surface, it does not open one.

local_refusals.description: Refusal codes this service emits that are not kernel codes, each mapped to the kernel refusal it realizes. A local code used by an operation and absent here is a defect.

logical_endpoint.description: Transport-neutral address of this operation. Always sov://<service_id>/<operation>; a transport is bound to it in contracts/capability-offices.json, never here.

subject.description: The record in this service's `owns` list that the operation acts on.

crud.description: The append-preserving CRUD verb. CREATE appends a new record. READ derives without writing. SUPERSEDE adds a later version and preserves the earlier one; it never overwrites. COUNTER adds a counter-record and never erases. REBUILD discards and recomputes a projection only.

requirement.description: The PRD requirement this operation serves, when it serves one directly. The id must appear in PRD.md; a later-phase id is well formed but not yet carried, and fails the check rather than passing quietly.

kernel_transition.description: The transition in contracts/kernel-transitions.json this operation realizes, when it realizes one.

commit.description: What a satisfied operation produces. A READ commits DERIVED and writes no authoritative record.

also_reads.description: Further records this READ returns alongside its subject. A record read through its parent is declared here rather than assumed; only a READ may declare it, and every entry must be a record the service owns.
